mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in <60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is in a sustained downward trend over 6 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates above 7.8% in a month signal labor market stress, leading to bearish sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns not negative when UNRATE crosses above 7.8% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in federal funds rates and rise in GDP demand (GDPC1) over a month create a positive feedback loop, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuations, driving 20-day S&P 500 returns upward.
candidate_trigger: Both FEDFUNDS down and GDPC1 up in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not positive when FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 move in tandem over a month.

mechanism_narrative: Strong supply growth (INDPRO) indicates robust production and corporate profits, boosting investor confidence and driving 20-day S&P 500 returns upward.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not positive when INDPRO is in a sustained upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in jobless claims (PAYEMS) below 135,000 in a month signals recession risks, causing market panic and negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns not negative when PAYEMS falls below 135,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising demand (RSAFS) combined with falling federal funds rates over a month creates a favorable environment for equity growth, lowering discount rates and boosting valuations, driving 20-day S&P 500 returns upward.
candidate_trigger: Both RSAFS up and FEDFUNDS down in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not positive when RSAFS and FEDFUNDS move in tandem over a month.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing inflation (CPIAUCSL growth below 2% in late-cycle) suggests peak inflation, prompting central bank rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL 12-month growth rate < 2% over a quarter
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns not negative when CPIAUCSL growth slows below 2% in late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates (>4%) and elevated unemployment (>7.5%) in a tightening cycle signal economic contraction, prompting risk aversion and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns not negative when both FEDFUNDS >4% and UNRATE >7.5%.
